title: How I use parallel agents to do AI game dev
author: MostBlood7319
selftext:
This is Pip, a cute platformer I started yesterday. The video shows the game after one day of development.

I originally designed the character about a year ago for a Tamagotchi-style game, but never got around to building it. Since Astra dropped, I’ve been experimenting with rapidly prototyping games, so I decided to bring Pip back and try making a platformer.

I’m building it with Kite3D, an open-source game engine I recently made using Three.js. The editor runs in the browser, and every game project is a normal Git repository. That means I can run four agents in parallel using Git worktrees. Each agent gets its own isolated branch and browser editor, where it can run, inspect, and debug its part of the game through the CLI.

Right now, I have a main agent working on the core player movement and animations, with three other agents focused on:

* Enemies
* Pickups
* Level design

For design stuff, I used GPT image to go back and forth on concepts, and once I was happy with them, I gave them to Astra as reference. 

Let me know if you guys have any questions!

comments.author: insanetheta
comments.body: Can you speak a little more to your asset pipeline?  Are you using asset packs for terrain or is everything procedural?

replies.author: MostBlood7319
replies.body: Everything is procedural, I didn't use any asset packs. The only asset I started with a was a PNG of the Pip character I already had.

comments.author: RecordingTechnical86
comments.body: Very cool. Will have to look into using multiple agents at once

replies.author: MostBlood7319
replies.body:
It can get expensive, but it makes things a lot faster, and it feels like you're running a mini game dev studio. 

I'm looking for feedback on the engine I made (it's open source). If you're interested in trying it out, check out our discord:

comments.author: DirtyMudder92

replies.author: MostBlood7319
